newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-HILL SIGNS FOR FOOTWORK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HILL SIGNS FOR FOOTWORK.

text.p: Briton Damon Hill stunned most Formula One observers on Friday when he revealed he had signed for the Footwork Arrows team for next year.

The world championship leader, who needs just one point to clinch the world drivers' championship next month in Japan, said he had made his decision on Thursday after a lengthy visit to the team's base in Oxfordshire, England.
Hill, given notice by manufacturers' champions Williams earlier this month that he would not be required by the team again next season, said he was delighted with his decision.
He turned down offers from both the Stewart and Jordan teams to accept what he described as "an excellent all-round package" offered by Footwork Arrows.

Hill said: "Tom Walkinshaw is an archetypal racing man -- a championship driver, the man I and others credit with turning around Benetton's fortunes and of course the successful head of an internationally-recognised design, engineeering and manufacturing group.
"Tom has offered me much more than I had hoped for -- a rewarding package, a great challenge to work with him and the chance to win some races in the future."
Hill said that during his tour of the team's factory he had reached his decision to accept their offer, leaving less than 24 hours for the announcement to be made before the end of the week.

Walkinshaw's pedigree includes having been engineering director of the Benetton team which won the world title with Germany's Michael Schumacher in 1994 and since then a successful spell in rebuilding the Ligier team in France before purchasing Footwork earlier this year.
Walkinshaw said he had first made contact with Hill after the Italian Grand Prix.

"It goes without saying that I am delighted that Damon has agreed to join TWR Arrows. Considering the other attractive options available to him he has obviously recognised the enourmous potential of our team," Walkinshaw said.

"Damon's abilities are beyond question. He stands on the verge of his first world title and he is a proven winner over several seasons with 20 wins from 66 grand prix starts -- an outstanding strike rate."

The Footwork-Arrows team are expected to announce at the Japanese Grand Prix in Suzuka on October 13 a new techincal partnership with engine suppliers Yamaha and next season will be using Bridgestone tyres.
These factors are understood to have convinced Hill that the Footwork team offered him the brightest future.
However, one firm of British bookmakers, who rate Hill at 1-9 to clinch this year's world title, make him a 33-1 long shot to win the crown next season with his new team.
